clue.text: A felonious agent disrupted intergovernmental organisation

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal spy has thrown an international body into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' looks like the agent's verb but signals that all fifteen letters of A FELONIOUS AGENT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The League formed after the First World War was a body through which governments cooperated, the forerunner of the United Nations.

clue.text: One royal nearly made a lot of ships

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

indicators.note: nearly means stopping just short, so the word made loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family has almost built a fleet of vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the last letter from 'made', leaving MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Film cast able, without feet, to dance naked!

indicators.note: the foot of each word is its last letter in this down clue, so cast and able each lose their final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the dance loses its outer letters

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking dance of Parisian music halls

explanation.surface: A saucy production note: the cast, though footless, must dance in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without feet' takes the last letters off 'cast' and 'able' (CAS, ABL); 'naked' strips the cancan to ANCA. 'dance' is not the anagram signal it appears to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is the 1942 Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman movie classic.

clue.text: Sloped gardens in Kent sold at last

indicators.note: in places the gardens inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: Kent lies in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word sold

explanation.surface: A garden sale in Kent took place on sloping ground.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic garden in London; Kent, an English county, is in the South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: Something skewed is set at a slant, tilted off the straight, just as a sloped surface is.

clue.text: Extra named Dud cast

indicators.note: to cast is to mould or throw into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film extra called Dud has been given a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as casting an actor but signals an anagram of NAMED DUD.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is something additional appended to a book or document, a supplement.

clue.text: Instrument has nothing on tenor

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
Alfie Boe is a well-known English tenor

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is no match for a tenor's voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has nothing on' reads as 'is outclassed by', but it is O placed on top of BOE: Alfie Boe is an English tenor, famed for musicals such as Les Misérables.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: More than half of biscuit dunked in that man's — sort of — tea

indicators.note: a biscuit dunked in tea goes inside it, so these letters sit within the pronoun

parts.note: that man's means his

indicators.note: more than half of the word biscuit means its first five of seven letters

explanation.surface: Someone dunks most of a biscuit in his cuppa, a slightly odd brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than half of' keeps five of the seven letters of 'biscuit'; the dashes set 'sort of' apart as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibiscus flowers are dried to make a tart, red herbal infusion drunk hot or iced.

clue.text: See seven are made poorly eating supermarket crabs, for example

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the supermarket goes inside the rearranged letters
made poorly means put together badly, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Seven people fell ill after eating supermarket crabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made poorly' rearranges SEE SEVEN ARE into VENERE...SEASE, and 'eating' takes in ALDI. 'crabs' is not seafood but pubic lice.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, or pubic lice, are a sexually transmitted infestation, an example of an infection passed on by sex.

clue.text: Packing touring chest after time finally set aside

indicators.note: the touring piece comes after the letter from time
finally points to the last letter of the word time
touring means going round, so the word for packing goes around the chest

parts.note: someone packing is carrying a gun, so armed
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Someone packs a travel trunk after the time is up and puts it to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packing' means carrying a weapon, not stuffing a case, and 'chest' is a box rather than a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked funds are reserved or designated for a particular purpose, set apart from the rest.

clue.text: Sort of brown insect eats midge, missing odd bits

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the insect surrounds what is left of midge

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of midge leaves its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A brownish insect gobbles up part of a midge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing odd bits' leaves I and G from 'midge', which 'eats' puts inside BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale sandy fawn, one of the lighter browns.

clue.text: Ava Gardner initially returns carrying posh fruit

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the reversed letters enclose the posh letter
returns means goes back, so the name and initial are read in reverse
initially points to the first letter of Gardner

parts.note: U stands for upper class, so posh

explanation.surface: The film star Ava Gardner comes back with some upmarket fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AVA G into GAVA, and 'carrying' puts U inside it. U for upper-class is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white pulp, grown in Central America and Asia.

clue.text: Warning: whore, regularly found on live stream

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word whore, starting with the first

parts.note: to live is to be
a tide is a current or stream of water

explanation.surface: A notice that prostitutes keep turning up on a live stream online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live stream' reads as an online broadcast but splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mock-solemn threat that trouble awaits someone, an exclamation of warning.

clue.text: One wept after heartless Etonian's given power

indicators.note: the weeping comes after the Etonian part
heartless removes everything but the outside letters of Etonian

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
to bleed is to weep in the sense of oozing, so bled is wept

explanation.surface: An Eton schoolboy, callous and empowered, has made someone cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves E and N of 'Etonian'. The 's is read as 'is' joining wordplay to definition. Eton is the elite English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enabled is to be authorised or made able, to have capability conferred.

clue.text: The Spanish half-heartedly taxied back to find disaster

indicators.note: back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: the middle of the word for taxied is a doubled letter, and only half of that pair is removed

parts.note: to cab is to travel by taxi, so taxied is cabbed

explanation.surface: A Spanish cab ride went wrong, the taxi reversing into calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: CABBED loses one of its central Bs to 'half-heartedly', giving CABED; 'back' then reverses ELCABED.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating failure or collapse, a fiasco.

clue.text: Report describing end of Stein's quite fancy dining

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line around, so the noise surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a report is a loud noise such as a gunshot, a bang

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of Stein
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of quite are rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of Rick Stein's rather elaborate restaurant meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a loud noise, not a write-up. Rick Stein is a British TV chef; the 's joins wordplay to definition as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banqueting is feasting at a grand formal meal, an elaborate kind of eating.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep in Corfu tonight

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asking where to sleep in Corfu tonight, a holiday problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Corfu' into 'tonight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress that unrolls on the floor or folds on a frame as a bed.

clue.text: Forty crews too disorganised

indicators.note: disorganised means lacking order, so the letters of crews and too are rearranged

explanation.surface: Forty crew members are in disarray as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorganised' rearranges CREWS TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so two of them make forty.

clue.text: Behind tramp

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side; 'Behind' is a noun, not a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for the backside and, in American usage, for a homeless loafer.

clue.text: British adore eating one at Trump's talk — in a grandiose fashion

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for adore surrounds the next letters

parts.note: to adore is to love
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Brit loves dining at Trump's place and hearing him speak pompously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's' is a link that nods to the former US president, often accused of this kind of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloviate is to speak at length in a pompous, windbag manner, an Americanism.

clue.text: Bunch of scientists left sounding adenoidal

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, employs a body of scientists

explanation.surface: A group of scientists departed, speaking through their noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' belongs to the definition, not a sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged adenoids block the nose, so the voice they produce is nasal in tone.

clue.text: Online shop? First save peeled fruit

indicators.note: first means the peeled word comes before the shop
peeled removes the skin, here the outer letters of save

parts.note: Ocado is a British online grocery retailer

explanation.surface: Grocery shopping online: first save money on some peeled fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' leaves AV from 'save'; 'First' puts it ahead of OCADO, a UK internet supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, with buttery green flesh.

clue.text: Hi, I undo buckles

indicators.note: buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting from someone who unfastens straps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckles' rearranges HI I UNDO, and the whole clue is the escapologist introducing himself as he slips his restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the famous escape artist who freed himself from straitjackets, chains and buckled restraints.

clue.text: Top cricket game in garden

indicators.note: in places the cricket game inside the gardening verb

parts.note: to garden is to hoe
ODI stands for one-day international, a form of cricket match

explanation.surface: The best cricket match is played in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a garment, not 'best'; 'garden' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded sweatshirt is a casual top worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Hormone; take second in time for smear

indicators.note: take the second means remove the latter of the two occurrences, so only the final pair goes

parts.note: insulin is the hormone that regulates blood sugar

explanation.surface: Instructions for an injection: take the hormone a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The hormone holds two INs; 'take second' removes the latter. 'in' is the letters removed, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear someone is to defame them, an attack on their reputation, an affront.

clue.text: Disguised in company — go outside idiot!

indicators.note: outside means the word go goes around the idiot

parts.note: a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone in a group, hiding identity, is told by a companion to step outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go outside idiot' reads as an insult hurled at someone, but 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their true identity, under an assumed name.

clue.text: Nerd's language not right

indicators.note: not means without, so the right letter is taken out

parts.note: Greek is a language

explanation.surface: A boffin's speech is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: GREEK loses R. The 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A geek is an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, often for computers.

clue.text: Sample a bit of Seurat visiting gallery

indicators.note: visiting means being inside, so the letter goes within the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the group of art galleries in London and elsewhere

indicators.note: a bit of Seurat here means its first letter

explanation.surface: Sample a little of a Seurat on show at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: S, 'a bit of Seurat', goes inside TATE, Britain's national gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a little of it, as a sample.

clue.text: Nightingale, famously put game back within three points

indicators.note: within places the reversed game inside the compass points

parts.note: N, S and E are three points of the compass

indicators.note: put back means the game's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A game played back inside three points, perhaps a sports report.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale nursed soldiers in the Crimean War; RU, rugby union, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale was the founder of modern hospital care, the celebrated Lady with the Lamp.

clue.text: Shapes Tarantino's first Salinger adaptation

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Tarantino
an adaptation reworks a story, so the letters of Salinger are rearranged

explanation.surface: Quentin Tarantino's debut film is based on a J D Salinger novel.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus the rearranged SALINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are three-sided figures in geometry.
